name: Masterclass question in every interview
evidence: Masterclass posts reached 3.3 times the month's median on LinkedIn (6 posts, June to September). Lori Goode's drew 37 comments, the second most of September.
adherence: Kept in every new question set from September.
next_step: Keep. Masterclass Off Duty episodes are booked to Dec 2.

name: Static news carousel (Industry Movers & Shakers)
evidence: 27% of people who see it click, against 4% for the median post. Reach is about average (0.9 times the month's median).
adherence: Every two weeks; booked to Dec 25.
next_step: Keep, and use it when the goal is clicks rather than reach.
source: LinkedIn analytics, 4 posts Aug 21 to Oct 16

name: Partners repost with their own words
evidence: Two partner reposts took posts to 8.2 and 7.7 times their organic engagement. Across all September posts the lift was 1.28 times, because most posts had none.
adherence: Most posts still get no partner repost.
next_step: Ask on every post; the nominee repost test (from Oct 26) tries it on nominee posts.

name: Instagram collab posts with the guest or brand
evidence: September's three best Instagram posts were accepted collabs. In October the Top 20 carousel, tagging about 30 brands, reached 4,075 accounts; single-guest reels had a median reach of 198.
adherence: Standard on honoree and partner posts, rare on guest reels.
next_step: The guest reel collab test (from Oct 26) extends it to guest reels; read it with the event reel test.

name: Soundbite hook opening on reels
evidence: View-through rose from about 34% to 40–44% on hook-format reels. It lifts reach, not how long people stay.

name: Newsletter subject lines in Title Case
evidence: Title Case beat lower case on opens. Exception: when the subject line starts with a celebrity's name, lower case won.
adherence: Standard from Sep 1; the exception lives only in notes.
next_step: Write the celebrity-name exception into the newsletter checklist.
source: beehiiv A/B test, Jul 22 to Aug 31

name: Short YouTube ad cut
evidence: The 30-second cut drew 32,881 views at 85.7% average viewed; the 203-second cut drew 8,527 at 34.5%.
adherence: Applies to the next paid flight.
next_step: Lead with short cuts in any future YouTube flight.

name: Links in the LinkedIn first comment, not the post
evidence: Within each post type, no link placement wins: guest interviews with the link in the first comment ran at 1.2 times the month's median, against 2.5 times with the link in the post (4 posts) or with no link (25 posts). Post type drives reach far more than link placement.
adherence: Since Jul 20, 45 of 158 posts put the link in the first comment, 33 in the post and 80 had no link. In October, 23 of 52 had the link in the post.
next_step: Stop policing placement; link every cut to its episode, with a content tag per post so site visits can be read.
source: LinkedIn analytics and comments, May 1 to Oct 24

name: Leadership quote posts
evidence: Did not reach or engage as hoped through August and September.

name: Week in Review
evidence: Pruned in July as a low performer.

name: ESPY's Spotlight
evidence: The most entries of any series in August (9) and no top-eight post on either platform.
next_step: Decide whether to retire it or rework it before next ESPYs.

name: Rewritten LinkedIn bio
evidence: Early read: Oct 1–24 drew 150 new followers and 704 page views, against 109 and 513 for Sep 1–24. Impressions also rose 18% (45,601 against 38,588), so part of the gain is volume; follows per 1,000 impressions rose from 2.8 to 3.3, the same gap as at Oct 23.
next_step: Read the full month on Nov 1.

name: Instagram captions end with "Watch the whole conversation at the link in our bio"
evidence: Link taps over 28 days went from 8 (to Oct 4) to 13 (to Oct 17).
next_step: Read link taps and site visits from Instagram at the end of October. Link taps are not in the Supermetrics pull, and the pull cuts captions at 160 characters, so both the result and whether captions follow the rule need a check in Instagram Insights.

name: Subscribe prompt moved up the homepage
evidence: Not readable yet: the measure is homepage visits that turn into signups, and beehiiv is not connected.
next_step: Connect beehiiv, then compare October's signup rate with September's.

name: One Top 20 nominee post a day on LinkedIn, with a repost ask to each nominee
evidence: Number to beat: a median 239 impressions per nominee post (22 posts, Oct 6–22). The 16 nominee posts of Oct 12–23 had a median of 221, and Oct 19 carried four.
adherence: Starts Oct 26; no posts from the test period are in the data yet. The last nominee post before it went out Oct 23, alone that day.
next_step: Read after voting closes Oct 30: median impressions of nominee posts Oct 26–30 against 239, and how many nominee brands reposted (the Reposts list; reposts are not in the Supermetrics pull).
source: Weekly briefing, week of Oct 26; LinkedIn analytics

name: Guest reels as Instagram collabs, plus one tagged vote carousel
evidence: Numbers to beat: a median reach of 198 for single-guest reels (Oct 6–22); the Oct 6 Top 20 carousel (4,075 reach and 24 shares when set; 4,082 now).
adherence: Starts Oct 26; no posts from the test period are in the data yet. The Oct 23 vote post was a reel (reach 331), not a tagged carousel. The Supermetrics pull does not show whether a post is a collab, so check that in Instagram.
next_step: Read on Nov 2: reach of the two collab reels against 198, and carousel reach and shares against the Oct 6 post.
source: Weekly briefing, week of Oct 26; Instagram Insights

name: Re-sharing LinkedIn posts a few days after they go up
evidence: Tried in May; no result on file and no record of whether it continued.
next_step: Decide whether to test it properly or drop it.

name: Recap carousels (documents) on LinkedIn
evidence: The June audit found document carousels drew a 32% median engagement rate, against 10.2% for video and 7.2% for images. Only the news carousel has followed.
next_step: Test one event recap as a document carousel.
